headlines.title: Woman dies after being stabbed in San Jose
headlines.description: A woman died after being stabbed in San Jose Friday, the police department said Saturday. Police said they responded to a report of a suspicious circumstance at around 1:50 p.m. in the 700 block of Linda Vista Street. At the scene, officers found an unconscious and unresponsive woman with unknown injuries inside a home, authorities said. The police department said the woman was pronounced dead at the scene. Evidence at the scene determined the woman suffered from at least one stab wound, according to authorities. Authorities said it was determined the suspect, another woman, and the victim knew each other, but added the motive and circumstances surrounding the incident are under investigation.

headlines.title: Bay Area community joins in prayer for those impacted by Nepal floods
headlines.description: On Friday, a Bay Area community came together to pray for those caught in the devastating flooding along the border of Nepal and China’s Tibet region. Dozens gathered at the Nepali Community Center in Richmond to light up candles and pray for families caught in the catastrophic flooding along the border between Nepal and China’s Tibet region. Nepali authorities say 626 people have died, and 2,426 others remain missing. The flooding has devastated communities along the border leaving families across the region desperately searching for news. natural disasters Aug 27 natural disasters Aug 28 milpitas Aug 27 The Nepali Association of Northern California says several of its members have family in the area. Although most have heard from their loved ones, the group says one family is still waiting. The community is also racing to help survivors by raising money for relief and trying to figure out how to get critical supplies into an area where so much of the infrastructure has been destroyed. “Since the bridges are all gone and there is flooding in the rivers, it’s hard for the people to really get there and help the people in need so there are helicopters but there not enough and even the medical kits we are running tight on those,” Nepali Association of Northern California President Preetesh Karki said. In the Bay Area, community members say the Nepali community is not the only community hoping to hear from loved ones who remain missing, as some Tibetan and Indian residents also share that wait. People in the U.S. looking for information about family members in the region are being asked to contact the state department.

headlines.title: 49ers wanted to review police report before disclosing Shanahan crash, records show
headlines.description: Newly released public records are providing a clearer timeline of the communications between the San Francisco 49ers and Palo Alto police after the car crash that seriously injured head coach Kyle Shanahan. The records, first released to the Mercury News, are in response to a public records request NBC Bay Area filed and obtained Friday. The documents help explain why the 49ers waited 11 days to publicly disclose the June 14 crash. Two days after the crash, 49ers Security Director Larry Day emailed a police administrative assistant. Day requested the collision report and information about the other vehicle. Police provided information about the second vehicle that morning, but said the collision report was not yet complete. Six days later, Day followed up. When police told him they were checking the report’s status, Day responded: “We just wanted to review the report today before we release any information to the media.” Police notified the team on July 23 that the report was available. Kyle Shanahan Jul 28 Kyle Shanahan Jul 28 49ers Jul 27 The following day, a text to a police lieutenant from 49ers vice president of security, Jeremy Jones, states he needed to give the department “a heads up on our media release.” The 49ers issued their public statement the next morning. Days later, Jones texted police again after a state database incorrectly listed the other driver as responsible. A lieutenant responded: “I found the problem. We are fixing it.” Police later publicly confirmed Shanahan caused the crash. Shanahan has said he took his eyes off the road to retrieve a dropped cellphone and crossed into oncoming traffic. Palo Alto police have refused to publicly release the crash report that they gave the 49ers, saying only people who are “parties” to the crash can get the report. They told the Mercury News they released it to the Niners because they own the Tesla Shanahan was driving, so they are parties to the crash. Neither Palo Alto police nor the 49ers returned NBC Bay Area’s calls on Friday for comment.

headlines.title: Groups call on South Bay leaders to do more to help homeless population
headlines.description: Twenty community groups have signed an open letter to Santa Clara County and the city of San Jose demanding more be done to assist the unhoused population. The groups say the Here4You hotline isn’t connecting unhoused residents with services efficiently. They also want an end to encampment sweeps until there is adequate housing available, clearer communication on resources, as well as additional therapists and case managers. “You can’t move on to an apartment or anything if there’s not a case manager for you, and you can’t get mental health services if there’s no therapy,” Unhoused Response Group founder Shaunn Cartwright said. Separately, the groups claim that, according to the coroner’s website, the county is on pace to match last year’s homeless population death toll, saying 99 people have already died on the streets this year. Santa Clara County Board of Supervisors President Otto Lee said he’d like to prioritize more short-term housing right away. “That’s 99 people living in our community that could not survive, and that shows that our system is falling short,” he said. Matching last year’s homeless death rate would still mean a lower total than previous years.

headlines.title: Police investigating shooting at San Francisco's Mission Bay neighborhood
headlines.description: Police were investigating a shooting in San Francisco. The shooting was reported 4:17 p.m. Friday at Fourth and Channel streets in the Mission Bay neighborhood. When officers arrived at the scene they found a male juvenile suffering from a gunshot wound, authorities said. The victim was taken to a hospital for non-life threatening injuries. No arrests have been made and no other information was immediately available. Anyone with information is asked to contact the SFPD at 415-575-4444 or text a tip to Tip411 and begin the message with SFPD.

headlines.title: Woman dies after hit-and-run crash in parking lot in Milpitas
headlines.description: A woman died after a hit-and-run crash in a parking lot in Milpitas Friday, according to the police department. Police said the crash was reported just after noon in the parking lot of Mill Creek Apartments, located at 440 Dixon Landing Road. Officials said witnesses reported seeing a blue SUV leaving the area immediately after the incident. Authorities said responding officers found a woman who had sustained significant injuries as a result of the crash. The woman was pronounced dead at the scene, police said. When searching the surrounding area, police said they found a blue SUV matching the witnesses’ description in a nearby parking lot. The vehicle also had significant damage consistent with being involved in a crash, according to authorities. The police department said the driver, a 32-year-old Milpitas resident, was arrested in connection with the incident. Authorities said this is an ongoing investigation.

headlines.title: Family mourns 81-year-old man killed in hit-and-run crash in Richmond
headlines.description: The family of the 81-year-old man killed in a hit-and-run crash in Richmond gathered on Friday to honor and remember him. The family of 81-year-old Rafael Delgado says the community has wrapped its arms around them in the wake of his death. On Friday, they gathered at the spot where the beloved father and grandfather was killed to honor his life, while hoping police find the driver responsible. Lucia Delgado, Rafael’s daughter, says losing her father still doesn’t feel real. Rafael Delgado was killed Sunday in a hit-and-run at 23rd Street and Hellings after leaving a nearby restaurant. “He was a very good example of what a father should be, a provider, a protector, a confidant and they took that from us that day,” Lucia said. Days later, the family is still waiting for answers and hoping for justice. The family says singing was Rafael’s passion and how he re-discovered joy after losing his wife 19 years ago this month. On the day he died, he was doing his daily routine: walking from his house to nearby restaurants to sing karaoke. He was on his way to a second restaurant when he was hit. Flowers now mark the chair Rafael always sat in at la Bahía de Jiquilisco, the last place he sang that day. Raquel, an employee, says he sometimes came more than once a day and always brought gifts. Starting Friday, the restaurant is holding a three-day fundraiser to help his family with expenses. Rafael was a father of six, a grandfather and great-grandfather. He would have turned 82 next week. His family will honor his life at a vigil and finding some comfort in the community that loved him. “It means that he was loved, it means that he impacted people in a way that we didn’t even know. It means that he had an influence in the community. It means that we are loved and not alone,” Lucia said.

headlines.title: Parents upset after unapproved press box at Pleasant Hill high school gets taken down
headlines.description: Several East Bay high school football players and their families were upset after a press box parents constructed during Spring Break was torn down by the school district on Wednesday. The press box was built in April after parents at College Park High School in Pleasant Hill after they claimed the school district ignored their request to build one for years. “I was here for the construction of it. I actually went inside the booth once it was built. It had marble countertops. It had a place for the visiting team, it had a place for the home team to do stats. It had a place for the announcer and scorekeepers,” But on Wednesday, the district took it down, just two days before the start of the season. Kids say they watched the destruction as they practiced for their first game. “They tore it down and kind of made our school and our players a little sad. I didn’t like how it made us feel,” high school football player Braylen Coleman said. Superintendent Dr. Adam Clark says he had no choice but to remove it. He says all structures over 6 feet high must be approved by the Division of State Architecture, a process that takes at least a year. “It wasn’t approved by the State Architecture, it wasn’t approved by our contractor, it wasn’t approved by our maintenance folks,” he said. “If it were to come down during an earthquake or if it were to catch fire then the liability is off the charts.” Parents say they understand some rules were sidestepped but they’re upset the district couldn’t find a compromise without tearing it down. Now, they’re hoping they can get the ball rolling to do it the right way. “Let’s get this process going. Let’s start doing what we need to do. Let’s sit down and have a conversation,” Carolyn Babcock, a parent, said. Kids and parents are trying to focus on the first game on Friday, hoping a permanent press box will be on the roster soon.

headlines.title: 3 South Bay residents killed in plane crash in Alaska
headlines.description: Three of the four passengers killed in a plane crash in Alaska Wednesday were from the Bay Area. The small plane crashed into the water next to a remote coastal town in Alaska. All four people on board were killed, including 65-year-old Ronald Schmidt and 20-year-old Lance Schmidt, both from San Jose. The oldest victim, 82-year-old Daniel Simons, was from Los Gatos. The pilot was from Anchorage, Alaska. The NTSB is investigating the cause of the crash.

headlines.title: These college degrees will net the highest salaries in the Bay Area
headlines.description: It will likely come as no surprise to college students that earning a technology-related degree will maximize one’s career salary in the Bay Area. The HEA Group, a higher education policy organization, released a study in which it estimated the average salary in California for students with various bachelor’s degrees. Topping the list was math and computer science. The study found that students can expect to pull in close to $140,000 in the first few years out of college. Computer engineering checked in at No. 2 ($125,120), followed by nursing at No. 3 ($123,693). Computer science ($123,528) and general engineering ($117,199) rounded out the top five. NBC Bay Area’s Scott Budman has more in the video report above.

headlines.title: San Francisco police make 58 arrests in drug enforcement operation
headlines.description: San Francisco police and sheriff’s deputies made 58 arrests during a one-day operation this week targeting drug markets in the city. Officers also seized over 122 grams of narcotics, which is roughly equivalent to the weight of a standard bar of soap, and hundreds of dollars in cash, police said. The Wednesday operation was coordinated by the Drug Market Agency Coordination Center, a task force that combines city law enforcement agencies like the San Francisco Police Department and San Francisco Sheriff’s Office to tackle open-air drug markets. Of the 58 individuals arrested, 54 individuals had arrest warrants, including 12 individuals taken into custody by the SFPD Fugitive Recovery Enforcement Team, which focuses on tracking down individuals with active arrest warrants, according to police. Police say the operation primarily took place on the Market Street corridor and in the city’s South of Market and Tenderloin neighborhoods. The arrests are part of a larger departmental initiative to prioritize breaking up open-air drug markets in the city. San Francisco launched DMACC in May 2023 to target open-air drug markets and narcotics sales. In July, police made 76 arrests during a similar one-day operation.

headlines.title: Air quality authorities order South Bay landfill to reduce odors
headlines.description: The Bay Area Air District has ordered operators of a San Jose waste management facility to correct air quality issues and reduce odors. The Newby Island Resource Recovery Park, located in north San Jose, is a landfill and recycling center bound by Interstate 880 to the east and the waterfront Alviso neighborhood to the west. It is operated by Phoenix-based company Republic Services Inc. through its subsidiaries International Disposal Corp. of California, which oversees the landfill, and Browning-Ferris Industries of California Inc., which runs the recycling center. According to the order, issued Wednesday by the Hearing Board of the Bay Area Air District, the facility is responsible for hazardous gas emissions over the years, prompting odor complaints from neighborhoods in San Jose, Milpitas, Fremont, and Newark. The Bay Area Air District is the agency responsible for protecting the air quality in the region. The Hearing Board is a five-member body within the air district that can issue abatement orders to pollution-causing entities, in this case, the operators of the Newby Island Resource Recovery Park. A 2024 study by the air district found that the Newby Island facility was the major source of the odors that residents were complaining about. Hydrogen sulfide, a gas linked to headaches, nausea, and asthma, was the primary pollutant causing the odors, a news release from the district said. In December 2025, the district ordered the operators of the facility to install continuous emission monitors to track hydrogen sulfide, after an investigation revealed that they were underreporting pollution concentrations. Wednesday’s abatement order reiterates the need for continuous emission monitors and directs the operators to improve landfill inspections using drones to better detect methane leaks. Another requirement outlined in the order is to automate the landfill gas collection system and to install air pollution monitors along the perimeter of the facility. “Families in the South Bay have lived with persistent odors and uncertainty about what is in the air near their homes,” said Philip Fine, executive officer of the Bay Area Air District, in the news release. “This order establishes enforceable deadlines, stronger monitoring and clear consequences if Newby Island fails to comply.” Failure to comply with the abatement order will lead to further enforcement, and the district will separately assess fines for the violations that led to this abatement order. A spokesperson for the International Disposal Corp. of California said that the firm appreciates the air district and the Hearing Board’s focus on increasing transparency around air quality concerns and will comply with the order. “IDCC will continue working constructively with regulators, residents and local stakeholders to meet those requirements,” said spokesperson Yessica del Rincon in an email. “IDCC and the Newby Island Landfill provide an essential service to our customers and remain committed to operating the facility safely and reliably.” Previously, in 2022, International Disposal Corp. of California and Browning-Ferris Industries of California Inc. agreed to pay $210,000 to settle with the district over 30 notices of violation from 2014 to 2020 for non-compliance with air quality regulations at the landfill. The violations included landfill gas surface leaks associated with composting operations in 2014 and 2015, landfill wellhead positive pressure violations between 2015 and 2019, and gas collection shutdowns in 2019. The settlement also cited public nuisance violations based on odor complaints between 2014 and 2016.
